findings.summary: The F-21.9-6 procedure note, now in docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md, attributes the stale post-fixture-edit observation to the provider inventory cache, but every reconciliation invalidates that cache unconditionally, so the stated mechanism is false.
findings.detail: The note at docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md:396-403 says a verifier must issue a configuration save after a fixture edit because 'Otherwise the inventory cache still serves the pre-edit observation', citing this run's observation that a scheduled task at 15:20:23Z still produced RenderPassThrough (PassThroughReason=NoDisplayableValue) for the sparse movie and that the change only became visible after the additional save at 15:21:40Z. That causal claim is contradicted by the implementation. src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/LibraryReconciliationService.cs:139 calls InvalidateInventory() unconditionally at the top of every ReconcileAsync run, and the comment above it (lines 130-138) states this explicitly: 'Post-scan (Jellyfin library refresh), manual and periodic scheduled, and post-save all run through this path, so discarding the retained observation sets here makes the work this enqueued begin a fresh provider-read window instead of serving a set observed before the trigger.' The same contract is asserted by an existing test, tests/ArrTags.Tests/ReconciliationTriggerTests.cs:261-271, which loops PostScan, Scheduled and PostSave and asserts each one discards the retained observation sets. So a scheduled task after a fixture edit already invalidates the inventory and could not have served the pre-edit observation. The observation itself is plausibly real, but the mechanism is not the inventory cache. The explanation consistent with the code and ADR-022 is the durable reconciliation cursor: src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/LibraryReconciliationService.cs:151 sets usesCursor only for Scheduled and PostScan, and ADR-022 clause 6 (docs/decisions/ADR-022.md:105-113) states that the post-save trigger 'is deliberately excluded ... so it always enumerates from the start and leaves the cursor untouched', whereas a scheduled run resumes from the persisted anchor and is round-robin. A scheduled run that had not yet reached the sparse movie in the current cycle would therefore not re-render it, while the following configuration save produced a PostSave reconciliation that always enumerates from the start and did cover it. That is a materially different lesson for a verifier: the cursor's round-robin coverage (ADR-022), not cache staleness. The practical instruction (issue a configuration save after a fixture edit) remains functionally correct for the wrong reason, so this is a documentation-accuracy defect rather than a product defect, but it is an asserted claim about product behaviour on a current-state surface, it is check-docs-guarded, and AGENTS.md forbids claiming behaviour that was not verified. It cannot be waved through as stylistic, because a verifier acting on the stated reason would conclude the scheduled trigger does not invalidate provider reads, which is the opposite of ADR-018 clause 3 as implemented and tested.

tests/ArrTags.Tests/ReconciliationTriggerTests.cs:261-271 - asserts PostScan, Scheduled and PostSave each discard retained observation sets (ADR-018 clause 3)
src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/LibraryReconciliationService.cs:151 - usesCursor = source is Scheduled or PostScan (PostSave is excluded)
docs/decisions/ADR-022.md:105-113 - clause 6: the post-save trigger always enumerates from the start and leaves the cursor untouched; the cursor governs only scheduled and post-scan

findings.recommended_action: Correct the mechanism in docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md:396-403 (and, if the 21.9 live-verification report is still editable, in F-21.9-6): keep the practical instruction to issue one configuration save after a fixture edit, but attribute it to the ADR-022 durable reconciliation cursor (a scheduled run resumes from the persisted anchor and covers the library round-robin, while the post-save trigger always enumerates from the start) instead of to the provider inventory cache, and state that every reconciliation including a scheduled one already invalidates the inventory per ADR-018 clause 3. Documentation only; no product code changes.
